oewn-05318579-n.learner: the part of the body that you see with
examples: Her father lifted up his eyes, Jane was distressed, Elizabeth looked expressively at Lydia

oewn-05711254-n.learner: the attention you give to what you are looking at
examples: He waved his hand to catch her eye across the room.
A red hat in the shop window caught my eye.

oewn-08540894-n.learner: an area that is near the middle of a larger area
examples: The little boat was caught in the eye of the storm.

oewn-03313242-n.learner: a small hole or loop, like the one in a needle
examples: She could not get the thread through the eye of the needle.

oewn-01364330-a.learner: feeling, showing, or bringing joy and pleasure, especially made happy by something
examples: I am glad you are come, for there is such fun here!
I am glad it occurred to me to mention it

oewn-02576313-s.learner: willing and eager to do something or to help
examples: I would be glad to help you carry those bags.

oewn-05702756-n.learner: something that pulls you toward it and makes you want it, or that has the power to do so
examples: His temptation is not adequate to the risk.
he was not likely to be proof against the temptation of immediate relief.

oewn-07500421-n.learner: a wish to have or do something that you know you should not
examples: She felt a strong temptation to eat the last piece of cake.

oewn-00160440-n.learner: the act of trying to influence someone by making them hope for or want something
examples: The painting shows the temptation of Christ in the desert.

oewn-00008300-r.learner: partly, or to the amount of one half
examples: but the portrait is only half alive, and is felt to be even a little unnatural.
In ran Mrs. Bennet to her daughters' room, in her dressing-gown, and with her hair half finished

oewn-00966726-v.learner: to talk with someone and keep the talk going
examples: they are very pleasing women when you converse with them.
if he wished to converse with her, he might have better success.

oewn-13964158-n.learner: how far or how much something reaches
examples: the kindness of the late Mr. Darcy, though she had not before known its extent, agreed equally well with his own words.

oewn-05130681-n.learner: the length, area, or amount of space that something covers
examples: They entered it in one of its lowest points, and drove for some time through a beautiful wood stretching over a wide extent.
On the following morning he hastened to Rosings to pay his respects.
She then hastened away to her mother
She hastened to explain that she had meant no harm.

oewn-02554590-v.learner: to make something go forward faster, or to make it easier
examples: when that apprehension first got abroad, it hastened his journey.
The doctor gave her a drug to hasten the birth.
You wish to think all the world respectable, and are hurt if I speak ill of anybody.
though his pride was hurt, he suffered in no other way.

oewn-01796596-v.learner: to cause someone great pain of the mind, or to make them miserable
examples: Losing the farm hurt him so badly that he could not sleep for weeks.

oewn-00064414-v.learner: to cause trouble or pain to someone or something
examples: Those tight shoes will hurt your feet.

oewn-02126629-v.learner: to be the thing that is causing pain
examples: My tooth hurts when I drink cold water.

oewn-00261356-v.learner: to cause damage to something, or to have a bad effect on it
examples: Bad reviews hurt sales of the book.
After the long walk I hurt all over.

oewn-00178121-a.learner: seeming to show that bad things will happen
examples: The sailors thought it an unfortunate sign to set sail on a Friday.

oewn-00876672-v.learner: to try hard to get something done or accepted
examples: Bingley urged Mr. Jones's being sent for immediately

oewn-00767694-v.learner: to push or drive someone or something in a certain direction
examples: The farmer urged the cows through the gate.

oewn-00860463-v.learner: to push someone on or encourage them, especially by cheering and shouting
examples: The crowd urged the runners on with loud cheers.
